title: Source every factual claim
statement: Back every real-world claim, and every non-fiction text, with a recorded, reputable source, and check each claim against that source, never against what sounds plausible.
detail: The course content-integrity skill ranks sources for every external-world claim (an official agency, standards body, museum, university or primary research first, then a domain reference chosen for the course, then a named fallback) and records each one's title, publisher, URL, retrieval date, exact locator, bounded fact, scope boundary and content digest; search snippets, unsourced summaries, blogs and model memory cannot support a pass (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/tooling/ti-courseplans-2169d1f/skills/course-content-integrity/SKILL.md`). The cross-subject guidance warns that a vivid but factually loose passage risks embedding misconceptions that are hard to undo (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0137-science-social-studies-reencounter-guidance.qmd`), and the reading project requires reputable sources for every science-bearing object (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/HOTBUCKET.md`). The source is of the strongest kind available, and checking each claim against it is a check of its own.
against: The claim checker was not referenced by any known gate when it was found, so nothing enforced the rule.

test definitions for missing categories and qualifiers; - test ontology/category mistakes, unsupported mechanisms, causal overclaims, and contradictions; - flag teleology or conscious intent attributed to evolved traits or impersonal processes; - compare the claim with the frozen source boundary, not with what sounds plausible.

Examples of blocking shapes include defining a broad category as only one subtype, calling a process a body part, treating an animal as a producer, or replacing a causal definition with "most connected."

Anti-leak (kb-0064) means "you must read the passage to answer" — it does NOT mean the passage's own facts are sourced or true. A perfectly anti-leak item can sit on an unsourced machine-authored passage.
**Note:** you grade **anti-leak + G5 compliance**, not source truth.
